Such a crash should also be logged in the logcat. 

Please redirect everything to a file without any filters, then zip it and upload it here. If the zip file is too large (> 10 MB), then only upload the last few hours containing the crash _(remove anything unimportant with a text editor, everything that happened before the app started)._

```
adb logcat > /tmp/logcat.log

{ Wait approximately 10 seconds and press Ctrl + C to cancel. }

zip /tmp/logcat.zip /tmp/logcat.log
```

The crashes started on version 4.6 dev 3, since I still have a long time to make the game, I decided that I would update the project with Godot, but in the process of switching to dev 3, the game stopped working. 

If you remove the reference to "head.rotation.x" - then everything works fine. I don't understand what kind of magic it is.

I was also able to crash my Samsung Tab S7 - Android 13 / Adreno 650 using this MRP. 
As soon as I have more time, I will try [bisecting](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/reporting_issues/bisecting.html).

So I identified a few elements from the MRP which seem to trigger the crash:
- It happens on `Player.rotate_head()` indeed as identified by @SkanerSoft. It can be automated by adding that call in `Player._physics_process()` and the game will crash without requiring user input.
- It's related to the WorldEnvironment in `levels/1.tscn`. I tried to toggle various effects off like Fog and Glow but that didn't help. What did solve the crash is to change the background mode away from "Sky" (e.g. to "Clear Color"). Even with everything reset to default values and just background mode on "Sky" (without actually assigning a sky resource), it crashes.
- It's related to the SubViewport which the 3D scene (`levels/1.tscn`) is instantiated in. Running `levels/1.tscn` directly as the main scene doesn't trigger the crash.

The latter point seems to give credit to @Alex2782's stacktrace in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/113465#issuecomment-3658218519, which initially surprised Bastiaan and I as it's a crash in `RasterizerCanvasGLES3` (2D rendering). The Viewport is in a 2D UI scene with a SubViewportContainer, so maybe that's what's triggering 2D rendering? Though it could also be that Alex's stacktrace would be nonsensical like mine, but it does look more coherent at least.

Further, `glMapBufferRange()` is not throwing any errors. It should _only_ return null if it also throws an error. 

Accordingly, my theory is that some combination of effects is making the renderer get into an invalid state. Once OpenGL gets into an invalid state, it no longer makes any guarantees about behaviour.
